annotations.description: Chose Blue for Thriving Heath's color when the deck is clearly White/Black. The card reference shows multiple black cards (Tragic Slip, Durable Coilbug, Morkrut Banshee, Wakedancer, Disciple of Perdition) that the player might draw. Blue has no use in this deck. This effectively makes Thriving Heath a Plains that enters tapped instead of a dual land.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Blue as the color for Thriving Heath
annotations.betterLine: Choose Black to have access to the deck's secondary color, enabling casting of black spells drawn later

annotations.description: Declined to cast Tragic Slip on Distinguished Conjurer (1/2), a value engine that gains life on ETBs and has a flicker ability. Tragic Slip's -1/-1 cleanly kills it now before it can generate value. However, saving Tragic Slip for morbid (-13/-13) on a bigger threat later is a reasonable consideration.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting Tragic Slip
annotations.betterLine: Cast Tragic Slip targeting Distinguished Conjurer to remove the value engine before it can untap and start flickering creatures or gaining life. Morkrut Banshee in hand can serve as removal for larger threats later.

annotations.description: Timed out during postcombat main phase with 3 untapped mana and multiple castable spells available. The opponent just deployed Preston, the Vanisher alongside Distinguished Conjurer, building a dangerous flicker engine. Haiku Villain needed to develop their board to keep pace.
annotations.actionTaken: No response (timeout) — passed the turn without casting anything despite having mana and spells available.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Durable Coilbug or Disciple of Perdition for {1}{B} to develop the board, keeping {B} open for Tragic Slip if needed. Any board development here is important against the opponent's growing engine.

annotations.description: Distinguished Conjurer (1/2) blocks Disciple of Perdition (1/3), but the Conjurer dies while the Disciple survives (1/3 takes only 1 damage). This throws away the key engine piece that enables Preston's flicker combo for no value — the Disciple isn't even killed. Meanwhile Preston blocks the Soulcage Fiend fine either way.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked Disciple of Perdition with Distinguished Conjurer (which dies without killing the Disciple) and Soulcage Fiend with Preston.
annotations.betterLine: Block only Soulcage Fiend with Preston (kills it, Preston survives at 2/2), and leave Distinguished Conjurer unblocked or don't block with it. Take 1 damage from Disciple of Perdition, preserving the crucial Conjurer for the Preston flicker engine. Net life: 17 vs 17 but you keep your combo pieces intact.

annotations.description: Using Tragic Slip without morbid to kill a 1/2 Distinguished Conjurer, when saving it could enable a morbid-powered -13/-13 to kill Preston, the Vanisher (2/5) which is a far more dangerous threat. Preston creates token copies of flickered creatures and can exile nonland permanents.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Tragic Slip during combat to remove Distinguished Conjurer and push through 4 damage
annotations.betterLine: Hold Tragic Slip for a turn where morbid is active (e.g., after a creature dies in combat) to use the -13/-13 mode on Preston, the Vanisher, which is the much more threatening card on the opponent's board.

annotations.description: Cast Wakedancer (2/2 vanilla, no Morbid) instead of Bone Picker (3/2 flying deathtouch) when both cost similar mana. Flying and deathtouch are especially valuable against the opponent's Blessed Sanctuary generating 2/2 ground tokens and Preston creating token copies.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Wakedancer as a vanilla 2/2 for 3 mana
annotations.betterLine: Cast Bone Picker for {3}{B} (4 mana) to get a 3/2 flying deathtouch creature that can fly over Unicorn tokens and trade with any threat

annotations.description: GPT54 Sport passed priority in precombat main with 6 untapped lands and three castable spells, effectively ending their turn without doing anything. They have Blessed Sanctuary and Preston on board, making creature spells especially valuable. Faith's Fetters could lock down a threat and gain 4 life. Brightmare could tap a creature, gain life, and create a 2/2 Unicorn via Blessed Sanctuary. This wastes an entire turn of development.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting any spell, effectively ending the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Faith's Fetters on Durable Coilbug or Wakedancer to neutralize a threat and gain 4 life, then cast Brightmare with remaining mana to tap another creature, gain life, and create a 2/2 Unicorn token from Blessed Sanctuary. At minimum, cast at least one of the three available spells.

annotations.description: Blocked Durable Coilbug with the Unicorn Token instead of Wakedancer. Durable Coilbug has a {4}{B} recursion ability from the graveyard, so killing it in combat is less permanent than killing Wakedancer. Either way 2 damage gets through unblocked, but trading the token into Wakedancer would permanently remove a threat rather than one that can be rebought.
annotations.actionTaken: Unicorn Token blocks Durable Coilbug (which has graveyard recursion)
annotations.betterLine: Unicorn Token blocks Wakedancer (permanently removing it), let Durable Coilbug through for the same 2 damage

annotations.description: Passed priority in precombat main phase with 7 untapped lands and multiple powerful plays available. Emiel the Blessed (4 mana) creates a devastating engine with the existing Preston + Blessed Sanctuary board, and Faith's Fetters could neutralize the opponent's Bone Picker (3/2 flying deathtouch). The player essentially skipped their entire turn for no reason.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority with 7 untapped mana, ending the main phase without casting anything.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Emiel the Blessed for 4 mana, creating a powerful flicker engine with Preston and Blessed Sanctuary already on board. This would also trigger Blessed Sanctuary to create a 2/2 Unicorn token. Could potentially also cast Faith's Fetters on Bone Picker with remaining 3 mana (needs 4, so would need to sequence differently - cast Fetters first or just Emiel). At minimum, Emiel is an incredible play here.

annotations.description: With Emiel the Blessed on the battlefield, 3 untapped Plains, Preston the Vanisher, Blessed Sanctuary, and Brightmare all in play, GPT54 Sport declined to pay {3} to flicker Brightmare. Flickering Brightmare would have triggered Preston (creating a 0/1 Illusion copy of Brightmare), Blessed Sanctuary (creating a 2/2 Unicorn), and two Brightmare ETBs (tapping two enemy creatures and gaining life). This is a huge value play that was missed.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Emiel's flicker ability, wasting 3 available mana.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Emiel the Blessed targeting Brightmare for {3}, generating multiple tokens and ETB triggers with Preston and Blessed Sanctuary on the battlefield, while tapping down opponent's threats.

annotations.description: With 3 untapped Plains and Emiel the Blessed's activated ability available, GPT54 Sport could flicker Brightmare to trigger a powerful chain: Brightmare ETB (tap a creature + gain life), Blessed Sanctuary (create 2/2 Unicorn), Preston (create Illusion copy of Brightmare which itself triggers another tap + life gain + another Unicorn). This would generate 2+ extra tokens, tap down opponent's threats, and gain significant life, all while the opponent is at just 7 life. Instead, the mana went unused.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Emiel the Blessed, wasting 3 available mana.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Emiel the Blessed targeting Brightmare to flicker it, generating multiple ETB triggers through Blessed Sanctuary and Preston, creating additional tokens and tapping opponent's creatures to set up a dominant board position and likely lethal next turn.

annotations.description: Declined to pay {G/W} for Emiel the Blessed's trigger on a Unicorn token, missing two free +1/+1 counters. With 3 untapped Plains and no castable spells in hand (Faith's Fetters costs 4, Rambunctious Mutt costs 5), the mana would have gone unused anyway.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to pay {G/W} for Emiel's counter trigger
annotations.betterLine: Pay {W} from an untapped Plains to put two +1/+1 counters on the Unicorn token, making it a 4/4 for free

annotations.description: Passed priority in postcombat main phase with an unplayed land drop (Plains in hand) and castable Faith's Fetters (4 mana, 7 untapped lands). Faith's Fetters on Morkrut Banshee 4/4 would neutralize the opponent's biggest threat and gain 4 life, while the missed land drop is pure waste. With the opponent at 7 life and a dominant board, this delays closing out the game.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, ending the turn without playing the Plains from hand or casting any spells.
annotations.betterLine: Play Plains (free land drop), then cast Faith's Fetters targeting Morkrut Banshee 4/4 to lock it down and gain 4 life, setting up a likely lethal attack next turn.
